definitions.text: This energy is stored in a molecule in which atoms are bonded to each other.
This form of energy is released when a bond is formed and absorbed when it is broken.
Enthalpy (H) or heat content, is defined as the total amount of thermal energy stored in a compound. The unit of its measurement is kJ mol⁻¹.
Heat is a form of energy that flows from hot body to a cold body because of a difference in temperature.

In Chemistry, the standard enthalpy of reaction (ΔH°) is the enthalpy change when reactants in their standard states undergo reaction to produce products in their standard states. This quantity is called the standard enthalpy change or heat of reaction at constant pressure.
In Chemistry, any physical or chemical change under study may also be called a system.
Everything else which does not fall in this system is called the surrounding.
When energy is transferred from surrounding to the system, the change is called endothermic and it has a positive sign.
When energy is transferred from system to surrounding, the change is called exothermic and it carries a negative sign, Fig. (5.1).
Heat, which is evolved or absorbed during a chemical reaction, is called the heat of that reaction.
Chemical reactions in which heat energy is evolved are called exothermic reactions
those in which heat energy is absorbed are called endothermic reactions.
The energy absorbed by the reactant or product molecules in order to be converted into the transition state is called the activation energy (Eₐ) of the reaction.
A catalyst is thus, defined as a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself undergoing any permanent chemical change.
This process that occurs in the presence of oxygen is called aerobic respiration.
In certain organisms like bacteria and algae respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen and it is called anaerobic respiration.
During glycolysis one molecule of glucose is split into two molecules of pyruvate.
Lipids are a group of organic compounds which include fats, waxes, sterols, etc.

definitions.term: Bond strength and reaction energy rule
definitions.text: When weaker bonds are broken while stronger bonds are formed, the reaction is overall exothermic and vice versa.
A catalyst increases the rate of reaction by decreasing its activation energy.
The reaction is exothermic if the energy of the products is less than that of reactants and endothermic if the energy of the products is more them that of reactants.

fullMarks: For a system-and-surroundings answer, identify what is being studied as the system, then state what counts as the surrounding and which way energy moves.
For enthalpy questions, distinguish H (total enthalpy) from ΔH (change in enthalpy); state the sign and whether heat is absorbed or evolved.
For bond-energy numericals, write the balanced equation, show the bonds broken and formed, substitute the given bond energies with units, and give ΔH with its sign and unit.

For reaction-profile diagrams, label the Energy and Reaction coordinate axes, reactants, products, transition state and activation energy; show products lower for an exothermic reaction and higher for an endothermic reaction.
When comparing catalysed and uncatalysed profiles, draw both paths from the same reactant level to the same product level; make the catalysed peak lower and label the activation energies.
For a transition-state drawing, show the reactant bonds partly broken and product bonds partly formed, using dotted lines and clear labels.

For respiration answers, identify whether oxygen is present, name the products where asked, and state that respiration is exothermic; distinguish glycogen storage in liver and muscles from lipids as energy reserves.
mistakes: Writing that exothermic reactions have a positive ΔH. Fix: energy leaves the system, so ΔH is negative.
Confusing heat with enthalpy. Fix: heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference; enthalpy is a property of the system.
Saying bond breaking releases energy. Fix: bond breaking absorbs energy; bond formation releases energy.
Forgetting that the bond-formation term is negative when using the signed bond-formation energies given in a question. Fix: check how the data are stated before choosing the formula.
Drawing products at the wrong energy level on a profile. Fix: exothermic products are lower than reactants; endothermic products are higher.
Showing a catalyst changing the reactant or product energy levels. Fix: keep both levels the same and show the catalyst lowering the activation-energy peak.
Mixing up glycogen and lipids. Fix: glycogen is the main stored form of glucose in liver and muscles; lipids act as energy reserves.

shortTheory.question: What is the difference between enthalpy and enthalpy change?
shortTheory.answer: Enthalpy of a system is represented by (H) while the change in enthalpy which a system undergoes is represented by ΔH. The total enthalpy (H) of a system cannot be measured directly. However, the change in enthalpy ΔH brought about in a system can be measured comparatively easily.

shortTheory.question: Why is breaking of a bond an endothermic process?
shortTheory.answer: Breaking of bonds of H₂ and O₂ absorb energy (endothermic process) while making of bonds between H and O evolve energy (exothermic process).

shortTheory.question: Depict the transition state for H₂ + Cl₂ ⟶ 2HCl.
shortTheory.answer: H—H + Cl—Cl ⟶ [H···H···Cl···Cl]‡ ⟶ 2H—Cl. Show the transition state in brackets, with bonds breaking and forming represented by dotted lines.

shortTheory.question: What is the role of glycogen in our body?
shortTheory.answer: Glycogen is the primary storage form of glucose. It is stored in the liver and muscles.

shortTheory.question: Why does the reaction between atmospheric oxygen and nitrogen not take place under normal conditions, but occur in the presence of lightning?
shortTheory.answer: Nitrogen of the atmosphere reacts with oxygen to produce nitric oxide in the presence of lightning. This is because reaction is highly endothermic, so only lightning can provide enough energy for this reaction to take place.

shortTheory.question: Explain the difference between the terms heat and enthalpy.
shortTheory.answer: Heat is a form of energy that flows from hot body to a cold body because of a difference in temperature. We measure heat in joules. Heat is what we call the transfer of thermal energy. Contrary to this, enthalpy is an essential part of a system since it depends on the number of molecules present in that system, its chemical composition and its structure. Heat is not essential part of a system, it just comes and goes. When heat leaves or enters a system, it results in a change of enthalpy. At a constant pressure the enthalpy change is equal to heat evolved or absorbed.

shortTheory.question: Explain why formation of a bond is always an exothermic process.
shortTheory.answer: Since energy is needed to break a bond while energy is evolved when a bond is formed, such reactions take place always with the evolution of heat.

shortTheory.question: Explain activation energy, transition state and aerobic respiration.
shortTheory.answer: The energy absorbed by the reactant or product molecules in order to be converted into the transition state is called the activation energy (Eₐ) of the reaction. The transition state is shown at the peak of curve in Fig. (5.4). This process that occurs in the presence of oxygen is called aerobic respiration.
